purpose: Independent verification of the Python fixed-m WPE test (dm_fixed_smoothing.wpe_*), the fixed-b Bartlett sensitivity test and the dm.test.r.m emulation (amendment2.hln_rm_batch) against the CRAN ForeComp 1.0.0 functions dm.test.wpe.fb, dm.test.bt.fb and dm.test.r.m. Read-only: no production code, frozen file, seed, band or verdict is changed or re-recorded.

P.python: wpe_test / wpe_batch (M = floor(n^(1/3)), t with 2M df)
P.r: dm.test.wpe.fb(d, M = floor(n^(1/3)))  (explicit M; ForeComp default for Mopt unset is the same)

S.python: bartlett_fixed_b_test (M = floor(n^(1/2)), KV 2005 cubic critical value at b = M/n)
S.r: dm.test.bt.fb(d, M = floor(sqrt(n)))  (explicit M: ForeComp's own default is ceiling(1.3 sqrt(n)), which is a different method configuration and is NOT compared)

toleranceJustification.statistic: WPE: R forms the DFT by an explicit n x M complex matrix product (rounding error about n*eps ~ 1e-13 relative), Python by FFT (about eps*log n). Bartlett and HLN: both use divisor-n autocovariances, differing only in summation order (about 1e-14). A relative 1e-9 bound leaves five orders of magnitude of slack while being four orders tighter than any plausible methodological difference (a divisor n-1, a missing HLN factor sqrt((n-1)/n), or floor versus ceiling in M change the statistic at the 1e-3 to 1e-1 level).
toleranceJustification.pValue: pt and scipy.stats.t.sf are each accurate to about 1e-15 relative. The p-value error propagated from a 2e-9 statistic error is bounded by 2 * max density (0.4) * 1e-9, so an absolute bound of 1e-9 covers it. P-values use the absolute bound only.
toleranceJustification.criticalValue: Fixed-b critical value is a closed-form cubic in b: 1e-12 absolute.
toleranceJustification.reject: Reject indicators must agree exactly, except where the R p-value is within 1e-9 of alpha (or |t| within 1e-9 of the critical value): there the indicator is not determined by the tolerance and the case is reported as BOUNDARY, never counted as agreement or disagreement. At most 2 boundary cases are tolerated over the whole run; more would itself be reported as a finding.
toleranceJustification.degenerate: Constant or numerically constant differentials: R's variance is rounding noise, not a defined quantity. Rule: Python must return a non-valid state (statistic None) AND the R long-run variance, recovered as (sqrt(n)*mean/stat)^2 when finite, must be < 1e-12 * mean(d^2) or non-finite. Python returning a valid statistic where R's variance is non-negligible is a disagreement.

inputs.calibrationFixtures: all 12 amendment-002 calibration cells regenerated from the frozen seeds (cell c uses seeds seedBase + seedCellStride*c ...) with the amendment-002 generator; committed test uses the first 25 seeds of each cell, the one-off verification run uses all 5000 per cell and also compares R rejection counts with the committed calibration JSON counts for P
inputs.q14EvaluationInputs: the 100 seeds in PREREGISTRATION-AMENDMENT-002.evaluation-freeze.json, generated by the production Q14 generator accept_cases_g07._ar1 with the preregistration q14.nullSimulation parameters, plus the q14.ar1Differential series. Read-only. Agreement only; no verdict.

randomized.seeding: numpy.random.SeedSequence([masterSeed, scenarioIndex]) -> default_rng; 200 series per scenario
randomized.scenarios: n in {12, 20, 30, 60, 150, 300, 1000} x innovation/dependence in {AR(1) phi=-0.5 Gaussian, phi=0 Gaussian, phi=0.5 Gaussian, phi=0.9 Gaussian, phi=0.5 Student-t(3), phi=0.5 with drift mean 0.3}; plus structured edge cases (constant, near-constant, huge scale 1e9, tiny scale 1e-9, shifted level 1e6, n=2..5 where R and Python are both asked)

stopRule: Any disagreement outside the tolerances above is recorded as a finding with exact reproduction and work stops for owner review; no tolerance or production code is adjusted afterwards.
